## Notes

- The seal is intact: "Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test." The audit has no break (`breaks: []`), and the 3 exchanges match the 3 turns.
- `findings.json` has no findings, and every count is 0. The verdict is `pass`.
- Turn 1: `check_stock` got `{"sku": "teapot-set"}` and the result was `{"sku": "teapot-set", "left": 3}` (trace.jsonl:3, backend trace.jsonl:5). The reply "Yes, the teapot set is in stock, with 3 left." matches the result and User goal 2.
- Turn 2: `check_stock` got `{"sku": "blue-mug"}` and the result was `left: 12` (trace.jsonl:15, 17). The reply matches. The only problem is the performance row above.
- Turn 3: `lookup_order` got `{"order": "6210"}` and the result was `{"item": "teapot set", "price_eur": 80, "status": "waiting for stock"}` (trace.jsonl:27). This matches `state.json:15-19`. The reply "Order 6210 (teapot set, €80) is currently "waiting for stock." I can't see a shipping date or location from here." agrees with the result and meets User goal 1. `lookup_order` reads the local `state.json`, so turn 3 has no backend call, as `app.py:52-55` shows.
- Order 6210 says "waiting for stock" while the stock service has 3 teapot sets (`stock.json:2`). This is a data mismatch between `state.json` and `stock.json`, not something the agent got wrong: it reported the tool result as it was. RULES.md says nothing about updating an order's status, so I did not report it as an issue. The shop owner might still want to look at it.
- RULES.md:7 says never to share another customer's order. The app has no customer identity, and `lookup_order` returns any order for any number (`app.py:52-55`). In this test the tester said "my order 6210", so the records do not show a break of the rule. The records also cannot show who owns order 6210.
- Persona: every reply is 1 or 2 sentences, polite and direct, with no slang or jokes. No boundary topic came up, and no turn asked for a reservation, so `reserve` was not needed.
- `turn_tokens` limit (2000): the output tokens of all model sessions together were 124, 134 and 99 for turns 1-3, all under the limit. The direct OpenAI calls do not count toward this limit, and their usage is not known.
- Every case note was routed as `other` (trace.jsonl:12, 24, 35). That is right for these messages, which are not complaints.
- The test folder has no `app-state/` folder. I read the app state from `state.json` and `stock.json` in the project. The 3 case notes in `state.json:21-25` match the 3 turns.
- No `egress_denied`, `unseen_call` or `egress_not_in_discovery` finding exists.

I found one issue in test 20261117-153746-4a8d: turn 2 took **60.8 s**, and the `turn_seconds` limit is 30. The model's answer was ready in about 11 s. The rest of the time went to slow outside services. The stock lookup took 8 s, and the two case-note calls to the note model took 25 s each. The app waits for both note calls before it replies (`app.py:116-120`).

Turns 1 and 3 called the right tools with the right inputs, and the replies matched the results. All turns stayed under the token limit and fit the persona. The seal is intact, the audit shows no breaks, nookku found nothing, and a proxy saw every outside service.

Two things are not app issues, but you may want to check them:
- Order 6210 says "waiting for stock" while the stock service shows 3 teapot sets, so the order data and stock data disagree.
- `lookup_order` returns any order for any number, so the agent can't enforce the rule against sharing another customer's order. Nothing in this test broke that rule.
